title: What Spain's Startups Law Changed in the Entrepreneur Permit, Article by Article
excerpt: Law 28/2022 rewrote the entrepreneur chapter of Law 14/2013. Read side by side in the Official State Gazette, the two texts show exactly what moved: the permit's length, the ENISA report, the criminal-record rule, and a visa that disappeared.
keyTakeaway: Since the Startups Law, the entrepreneur permit is three years with a two-year renewal and permanent residence at five, the report comes from ENISA within ten working days, and the one-year preparatory visa of old article 68 no longer exists.
summaryEn: A field-by-field comparison of Spain's Law 14/2013 as originally published and as amended by Law 28/2022, using the two BOE texts, for the articles that govern the entrepreneur residence permit.

faq.q: Which text of Law 14/2013 applies to me?
faq.a: The consolidated text on boe.es, which already contains the 2022 amendments. The original 2013 text is useful only to see what changed, and some older guides still quote it.

faq.q: Did the Startups Law create the entrepreneur permit?
faq.a: No. The permit dates from Law 14/2013. Law 28/2022 changed how long it lasts, who writes the report, how fast, and how the application is filed from abroad.

faq.q: Is the one-year "entrepreneur visa" to prepare a business still available?
faq.a: No. That was article 68 of the 2013 text, and Law 28/2022 deleted it.

content:
Two documents on boe.es tell the whole legal story of Spain's entrepreneur permit. The first is Law 14/2013 as originally published in September 2013. The second is Law 28/2022, the Startups Law, published on 22 December 2022 and in force the next day, whose fifth final provision rewrote the chapter of the 2013 law that founders depend on. This article reads them side by side. We quote the gazette, not a summary of it, and everything was checked on 8 November 2026. If you want the text that applies today in one place, use the consolidated version of Law 14/2013; the original is here to show what moved.

Who the section covers

Original article 61 opened the international mobility section to five groups: investors, entrepreneurs, highly qualified professionals, researchers and intra-company transferees, and excluded EU citizens and people with EU free-movement rights. The 2022 law added a sixth letter, international teleworkers, and built a new chapter for them. Nothing changed for entrepreneurs here except the company they keep.

The general requirements, and one real change

Original article 62 set the conditions every applicant meets: not in Spain irregularly, at least 18, no criminal record in Spain or in the countries lived in during the last five years, not flagged for refusal in the Schengen area, public or private health insurance with an insurer authorised in Spain, sufficient means for yourself and your family, and the fee paid. Family could apply jointly: spouse, children under 18, and adult children unable to support themselves.

The 2022 law touched one letter. The criminal-record requirement now covers the last two years of residence, and is paired with a responsible declaration that there have been no convictions in the last five. The five-year horizon did not disappear; it moved from certificates to a signed statement. Consulates may still ask for more, as our guide notes, but the law's own wording is two plus five.

The permit's length: from silence to three years

Original article 69 created the residence authorisation for business activity, valid throughout Spain, and said nothing about how long it lasted; the general renewal rule in article 76 spoke of two-year periods. The rewritten article 69 is specific. The permit is valid for three years. After that it can be renewed for two years, and permanent residence can be obtained at five. The same article now says how the application is made: by the applicant or a legal representative, electronically, with the UGE; and, for a founder outside Spain, through a single application that starts the authorisation and then the visa, consecutively.

The report: from "the competent body" to ENISA, in ten working days

Original article 70 defined entrepreneurial activity as innovative with special economic interest for Spain, evidenced by a favourable report from "the competent body of the central administration". It told that body to weigh job creation in Spain first, then the applicant's profile, the business plan and the added value.

The 2022 text changes three things. The activity must be innovative and/or of special economic interest, so either limb will do. The report comes from ENISA, by name; the UGE requests it ex officio, it is mandatory, and it must be issued within ten working days. And the assessment criteria are restated without the "job creation first" instruction: the applicant's profile and involvement, with each partner assessed whether or not they need a visa; the business plan, with the project, the product or service and its financing, including the investment required and its possible sources; and the elements that add value for the Spanish economy, innovation or investment opportunities. A founder outside Spain applies for the visa once the permit is granted.

The visa that disappeared

Original article 68 offered a one-year visa to enter Spain for the sole or main purpose of carrying out the preparatory steps for an entrepreneurial activity, with a path from that visa into the residence permit. The 2022 law deleted article 68 outright. Any page still offering a "one-year entrepreneur visa to prepare your business" is describing a provision that no longer exists.

Two additions founders rarely hear about

  • Article 76.4, new. For the first six months of residence, a passport is enough to register with Social Security when the holder does not yet have a NIE. It is the reason you can start paying contributions before your card arrives.
  • Additional provision 21, new. Spain is to facilitate issuing the NIE to applicants under this law, with a dedicated web page for appointments. A promise in the law; check the ministry's pages for how it has been implemented.

Two more are worth a line. Additional provision 20 ordered instructions with the specific requirements for each visa and permit by 31 March 2023, and said the means thresholds would be referenced to the minimum wage (SMI). Additional provision 17 lets graduates at EQF level 6 or above stay up to 24 months after their studies to look for work or start a business.

What did not change

Article 76's core stayed: the UGE processes the file by electronic means, the Dirección General de Migraciones grants it, the maximum period to decide is 20 days from filing, silence means granted, decisions are reasoned and open to an administrative appeal. Article 75.5's consular deadline of 10 working days, with its exception for applicants subject to prior consultation under the Visa Code, is also the 2013 wording.

How to use the two texts

  1. Read the consolidated text for the rule. Read the original only to understand an older article, consultant note or forum post that quotes "the law" and seems to contradict it.
  2. When a source cites article 68, or a two-year permit, or a report from "the competent body", it is quoting 2013. Ask for the date.
  3. Both BOE pages carry a permanent ELI link. Cite that, not a screenshot.

Our Spain guide applies the current text to a real file, and the route finder tells you whether that file is yours to open.
